findings.title: Honor challenged by self-ranking
findings.claim: Iblis's repeated fire-and-clay self-ranking makes God's honoring of Adam the object of a dispute over worth.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb كَرَّمْتَ carries the act of conferring honor, while the relative phrase and عَلَيَّ frame Adam's standing against Iblis. In 7:12 and 38:76, Iblis says he is better than Adam and cites fire against clay; that comparison returns to the focus honor clause and recasts it as a grievance against value bestowed on another.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause reads as a conflict between received dignity and Iblis's self-measured superiority, rather than as a bare report of preference.
findings.containment: The wider accounts repeat Iblis's own argument; they do not endorse material origin as a valid measure. This finding stays with the honor dispute and does not absorb the separate jaw-control reading.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and KRM B001 core/extension are supplied directly, and the connections include exact Arabic. The reader-walk source is legacy_unbound, while the valued-person branch B010 is qualified and rests on one attestation, so that nuance remains bounded.

findings.title: Jaw bridle and faceward gathering
findings.claim: The focus's jaw-bridling image has a wider counter-image in the gathering of misled people on their faces in 17:97.
findings.mechanism: The focus word أَحْتَنِكَ is carried by the packet's nominated jaw-bridling image. The supplied 17:97 text gathers people on their faces, blind, mute, and deaf; its connection note marks an inversion. Contact between the jaw-directed image and this faceward scene makes the threat resonate with a loss of human orientation.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat's image of taking direction acquires a grim opposing picture of people brought face-first with their faculties disabled.
findings.containment: The packet does not say the threat in 17:62 causes the condition in 17:97 or that every descendant shares it. The two scenes remain a wider image-level counterpoint.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk nomination is legacy_unbound and the branch has only a nominated source-image facet. The focus occurrence and 17:97 Arabic are supplied directly, but the relation is retained as a counter-image rather than a causal sequence.

branch_activations.activation: The focus's jaw-directed image meets the wider faceward scene as an inversion of orientation and bodily posture.

findings.title: A bid to steer the descendants
findings.claim: The jaw-bridling image in Iblis's threat can be heard as an attempt to steer Adam's descendants through misleading promise and invitation.
findings.mechanism: أَحْتَنِكَ carries the nominated image of a rein at the jaw. The wider statements in 4:119-120 name misguidance and deceptive promises; 14:22 describes invitation followed by response, while 16:99-100 limits authority to those who trust or ally with Satan. Those contacts make the bridle's direction-bearing action a figure for influence that depends on following and alliance.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat becomes a program for redirecting human conduct, while the wider account leaves response and allegiance visible in the mechanism.
findings.containment: The focus still states an emphatic threat against the progeny. The wider passages describe how influence works and where authority is limited; they do not prove total success or turn the threat into literal restraint.

epistemic.reason: The focus occurrence and global target Arabic are supplied, but HNK B003 is a nominated source image without an independent lexicon identity, and the reader-walk source is legacy_unbound. The directional reading is therefore retained with attribution and a bounded claim.

branch_activations.activation: The rein's directional action meets the wider account of misguidance, invitation, response, and alliance, changing the threat into a bid to steer followers rather than a guaranteed grip on every descendant.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The threatened capture is legible as directional influence pursued through misleading inducement and answered by followers.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual reading of the stated threat; it does not establish its complete success or erase the focus's forceful claim.

findings.title: A reprieve with a fixed horizon
findings.claim: The delay invoked in 17:62 has the shape of a permitted interval with a stated endpoint: in the other supplied Iblis accounts, he asks for time, receives it, and is told its limit.
findings.mechanism: أَخَّرْتَنِي carries the act of putting Iblis off until a named day. The supplied accounts at 7:14-15, 15:36-38, and 38:79-81 repeat the request, the grant of reprieve, and the known-time endpoint; that sequence meets the focus verb and deadline and makes the delay legible as a bounded allowance.
findings.reader_payoff: The speaker's requested time is shown inside a permission whose duration and limit are set beyond him.
findings.containment: 17:62 remains Iblis's conditional threat and stated horizon; the parallel requests do not report the threat's success or make him the owner of the endpoint.

epistemic.reason: The focus morpheme and accepted delay facet are supplied, and each wider connection includes exact Arabic that states a request, grant, or endpoint. The reading rests on those direct surfaces and their packet notes.

findings.title: The unnamed few and the named exception
findings.claim: The focus leaves its few unnamed, while elsewhere Iblis names God's sincere servants as an exception to his reach; the repeated exception can give the bare count a possible qualitative echo.
findings.mechanism: The focus's إِلَّا قَلِيلًا carves out a small remainder without describing its members. In 15:40 and 38:83, the supplied Arabic uses the same exception frame for God's sincere servants. Their contact allows the numerical remainder to be heard alongside a status-defined exception, while leaving the identity open.
findings.reader_payoff: The small number may carry a question of allegiance as well as quantity, without the reader being asked to identify the groups outright.
findings.containment: 17:62 states only that a few are excepted. Neither supplied connection equates those few with the sincere servants or with the servants mentioned in 17:65; this remains an analogy between exception statements.

epistemic.reason: Both connections supply the exact repeated exception phrase, but the focus does not identify its members and no target morphology is supplied. The qualitative echo is retained without asserting identity.

findings.title: A lineage of answerable people
findings.claim: The descendants targeted as one family line also appear in the wider evidence as witnesses and individually answerable people.
findings.mechanism: ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ is the collective object of the focus threat. In 7:172, Adam's descendants bear witness concerning themselves; in 52:21, descendant relation is preserved while each person remains answerable for what they earned. Those contacts change the line from an undifferentiated object into a family of distinct agents with their own accountability.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat addresses a lineage, yet the wider picture keeps each person morally distinct within it.
findings.containment: These connections do not name which descendants are among the few or say that the threat fails; they limit any inference that descent makes the whole line a single accountable subject.

epistemic.reason: The focus word and both target Arabic surfaces are supplied, and the connection notes identify witness and individual-accountability relations. Target morphology is not supplied, so the claim stays at that contextual level.
